questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Other

questions.question: Please explain: *
questions.answer: I went to germany to improve my german.

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: The fact that it was a german-speaking city.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Very easy. I got a lot of help from the hosting university through the language course I attended.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I got a buddy and a supervisor at uni, and I was introduced to different aspects of uni life in the language course.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: A bit difficult. Would recommend starting the search very early and be prepared to spend a lot on accommodation.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: It's fine, but try to find something near campus or the city center. It is more fun.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Pretty bureaucratic, actually.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: You find the courses you would like to attend online in LMU's pretty confusing and outdated website. Then you ask each lecturer if you can attend the course. Then you attend them and see if they are something for you. At last you confirm that you would like to attend for the duration of the semester.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: My supervisor was of great help.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: 100% successful. It took a long time though.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Try out a whole lot of courses and take your time in deciding which one you would actually like to write your exams in. There is no rush.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The level was a little lower than in Copenhagen.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA courses at your host university? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: A little lower. The recommended amount of reading and preparation was not as high or demanding as in Copenhagen - but it was of course complicated by the fact that it was in german.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: More loose and less structured. The teaching was also more studentdriven, which was nice, but it also sometimes resulted in a more frustrating and confused classroom feeling.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Nach Auschwitz.
Gefallen am Verfall. 
Der zersplitterte Bildungsroman.
Theodor Fontane: Effi Briest. 
20th century american fiction, 1945-1965. 
Lost generation(s)? Beatniks und Pop-Poeten.

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Der Zersplitterte Bildungsroman with Viktor Fritzenkötter and Gefallen am Verfall with Mathias Löwe. The lecturers were amazing and were able to make class enlightening and fun at the same time.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: None, it was very similar to my life in Copenhagen.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Food and books were a bit cheaper.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I tried attending sports through uni, but all the classes were fully booked. I found that very annoying.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Not much. On paper you could do sports but not in reality. There weren't many cultural or social activities as well, but that did not matter much to me, so I'm not the best judge of that.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Definitely sports even though I did not succeed in attending. I figure a team sport would be a very good way to get to know people.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Visit the big lakes and castles around Munich. And visit Salzburg for a day or two and go to the opera.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very easy. German culture is basically identical with danish culture.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Stay after class and don't be afraid to ask people to drink coffee. And attend blockseminars because they are the best way to get to know people at uni.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: None.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The german politeness, actually.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Go in the summer. Don't be cheap, when looking for accommodation. Buy the Deutschlandticket and travel around Germany in your free time.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Have patience with the german bureaucracy.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Learning german and being able to speak it freely in the end.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Learning german...

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: no.

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
